Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and G3470; unblemished (literally or figuratively):--without blame (blemish, fault, spot), faultless, unblamable.
BiblicalUsage: God chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world, Paul says, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love — and Christ will present the church to himself glorious, not having spot or wrinkle, holy and without blemish. Peter calls Christ himself the lamb without blemish and without spot, and Jude closes his letter praising the One who is able to present us faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word holds the whole exchange of the gospel: Christ was without blemish so that we, who are full of them, can be presented without blame. It is not that God lowers His standard — it is that Christ meets it for us, and then His Spirit works the same cleanness into our lives day by day.
